t: In front of you is the Albert Memorial in Kensington Gardens, a Gothic Revival canopy rising 176 feet over a statue of Prince Albert, who faces south. Queen Victoria commissioned it in memory of her husband, who died in 1861. Albert had been consort since their marriage in 1840, and Victoria gave him the title Prince Consort in 1857. Sir George Gilbert Scott designed it, a prolific Gothic Revival architect of over 800 buildings. It took more than ten years to finish, and the £120,000 cost was met by public subscription. The Royal Albert Hall is directly south of you.
